propositions.text: The claimant is Mr. XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, a citizen of El Salvador claiming refugee protection in Canada under IRPA section 96 and paragraph 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: The claimant, Mr. XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, a citizen of El Salvador, is claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and paragraph 97(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, Mr. XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, a citizen of El Salvador, claims refugee protection in Canada under IRPA section 96 and paragraph 97(1)(b).

propositions.text: The claimant's allegations are summarized as they appear in his Personal Information Form (PIF).
propositions.quote: Here is a summary of the claimant's allegations, as they appear in his Personal Information Form (PIF).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's allegations are summarized from his Personal Information Form (PIF).

propositions.text: The claimant worked for a XXXXX XXXXX in El Salvador and was threatened to pay $100 monthly to Mara Salvatrucha gang members starting in 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant was working for a XXXXX XXXXX in El Salvador. In XXXXX 2008, he was required, under threat of death, to pay a monthly amount of one hundred dollars to members of the Mara Salvatrucha gang.

propositions.text: The claimant and family faced threats and intimidation; wife and children moved to Honduras; claimant left El Salvador in 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant and his family were subjected to threats and intimidation. His wife and children left to live in Honduras. The claimant left his country on XXXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant worked for a XXXXX XXXXX, was threatened by Mara Salvatrucha gang to pay extortion, family fled to Honduras, claimant left El Salvador in 2008.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction by exhibits filed on the record.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction by the exhibits filed on the record.

paragraphs.summary: The panel is satisfied the claimant's identity was established by exhibits filed on record.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claimant is not a person in need of protection or a Convention refugee after examining evidence.
propositions.quote: Having examined the documentary and testimonial evidence, the panel determines that the claimant is not a person in need of protection or a Convention refugee, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The panel determines the claimant is not a person in need of protection or a Convention refugee after examining evidence.

propositions.text: To benefit under IRPA section 96, claimant must show serious possibility of persecution on one of five Geneva Convention grounds.
propositions.quote: In order to benefit from protection under section 96, the claimant must demonstrate that there is a serious possibility that he would be persecuted if he were to return to his country, by reason of one of the five grounds under the Geneva Convention: race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership in a particular social group.

propositions.text: The claimant did not support his fear of persecution with evidence related to one of the five Convention grounds.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant did not support his fear of persecution with evidence related to one of the five grounds of the Convention.

paragraphs.summary: To benefit under IRPA section 96, claimant must show persecution on five grounds; claimant did not support fear with such evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant's evidence did not implicate El Salvador or its agents as persecutors; claim cannot be considered under IRPA paragraph 97(1)(a).
propositions.quote: The claimant's evidence did not implicate El Salvador or one of its agents as the agent of persecution. Accordingly, the panel finds that the claim cannot be considered under paragraph 97(1)(a) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's evidence did not implicate El Salvador or its agents as persecutors; claim cannot be considered under IRPA paragraph 97(1)(a).

propositions.text: Is the claimant at a higher personalized risk than the general population in El Salvador within Prophète meaning?
propositions.quote: Is the claimant at a higher personalized risk than that of the general population in El Salvador, within the meaning of Prophète?

paragraphs.summary: The issue is whether claimant faces higher personalized risk than general population in El Salvador under Prophète.

propositions.text: Claimant fears 15 Mara Salvatrucha members who operate in his neighborhood and extorted him due to his job position.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he fears 15 members of the Mara Salvatrucha, and that they operate in the neighbourhood where he was living. He knew them before they approached him in XXXXX 2008, when they allegedly began extorting from him. The claimant stated that he was approached because he held a position at a XXXXX XXXXX; it was therefore easier to obtain money from him.

propositions.text: Claimant said risk is same as other citizens; everyone is at risk of extortion and possible killing if they don't pay.
propositions.quote: When questioned as to whether he faced the same risk as other citizens, the claimant responded that the risk was the same and that everyone in the general population is at risk of being extorted by gangs. He added that citizens must pay, failing which they might be killed-this is what he fears.

propositions.text: Claimant said living elsewhere like San Salvador would not reduce risk; gangs are everywhere.
propositions.quote: When asked whether he could live somewhere else, like San Salvador, the claimant stated that he would be at risk of being extorted there as well, either by the Mara Salvatrucha or by the M-18, because the gangs are everywhere.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant fears 15 Mara Salvatrucha members who extorted him; risk same as other citizens; gangs everywhere including San Salvador.

propositions.text: Claimant's risk of extortion is same as other citizens; he was targeted because of his job.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the claimant's risk of being targeted and extorted is the same as that faced by other citizens of El Salvador. The claimant indicated that it was easier to target him because he worked for a XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's risk of extortion is same as other citizens; targeted because of his job.

propositions.text: Documentation shows El Salvador is one of the most dangerous countries with an epidemic of murders targeting young men.
propositions.quote: The documentation, in this case, tab 7.6 of the National Documentation Package on El Salvador, indicates that El Salvador is one of the most dangerous countries in the world. According to the World Health Organization's criteria, there is an epidemic of murders, and young men are the principal target of assailants.

paragraphs.summary: Documentation shows El Salvador is very dangerous with an epidemic of murders targeting young men.

propositions.text: About 100 gangs with 30,000 members kill, steal, extort; all society strata affected and all citizens at risk.
propositions.quote: There are about 100 gangs in El Salvador, comprising 30,000 members. They kill, steal and extort from anyone in order to be able to support their incarcerated associates and their family. Businesses and farming operations are extortion targets. Home burglary is becoming more prevalent, as is credit card cloning and kidnapping for ransom. Cyber crime also exists. The documentary evidence demonstrates that every stratum of society is affected and that all citizens are at risk of being victims of criminality.

paragraphs.summary: About 100 gangs with 30,000 members kill, steal, extort; all society strata affected and all citizens at risk.

propositions.text: Claimant's fear is generalized, shared by general population coping with criminality and gangs in El Salvador.
propositions.quote: In this context, the panel is of the opinion that the claimant's fear is a generalized fear that is also faced by the general population in El Salvador, who must live and cope with the torments of criminality and the consequences of the proliferation of gangs.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's fear is generalized, shared by general population coping with criminality and gangs in El Salvador.

propositions.text: Prophète case law confirms generalized risk does not constitute risk under IRPA paragraph 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: The issue of generalized risk is a principle that case law confirmed in Prophète. In that case, Honourable Madam Justice Tremblay-Lamer stated that, when in a country, the risk of being targeted by any form of criminality is general; this does not constitute a risk of being subjected to a risk to life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment under paragraph 97(1)(b) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Prophète case law confirms generalized risk does not constitute risk under IRPA paragraph 97(1)(b).

propositions.text: Claimant did not demonstrate on balance of probabilities a personalized risk greater than general population.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant did not demonstrate, on a balance of probabilities, that he faced a personalized risk and a greater risk than the population in general.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant did not demonstrate on balance of probabilities a personalized risk greater than general population.

propositions.text: Panel cannot allow claimant's claim under IRPA paragraph 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: As a result, the panel determines that it cannot allow the claim filed by the claimant under paragraph 97(1)(b) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Panel cannot allow claimant's claim under IRPA paragraph 97(1)(b).

propositions.text: Panel rejects claimant's claim; does not recognize him as Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: For the reasons previously provided, the panel rejects the claim filed by XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, and does not recognize him as a Convention refugee under section 96 or a person in need of protection under subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Panel rejects claimant's claim; does not recognize him as Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: Claim for refugee protection is rejected.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, his claim for refugee protection is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: Claim for refugee protection is rejected.
